newsitem.title: CANADA: Three senior executives quit at Arakis.
newsitem.headline: Three senior executives quit at Arakis.

text.p: Three of Arakis Energy Corp's top executives have resigned from the company, Arakis chief executive John McLeod confirmed on Friday.

Gone from the company's executive suite are prominent vice-presidents Peter Holstein, David Robinson and David Harrison, all of whom played large roles in events leading up to Arakis's recent announcement of a US$1.0 billion deal to develop its oil concessions in Sudan.
"I got a faxed resignation yesterday afternoon," McLeod said in an interview.
"I knew things were not happy and we planned some changes in there as well."

Arakis also said on Friday it would respond to a recent call from a large number of its shareholders by approving a share buyback. The company said the program would give management discretion to make purchases from time to time up to a total of 10 percent of Arakis's stock.

The company said it had about US$50 million in deposit and no immediate need for the cash. "In the opinion of the board of directors, the common shares are an attractive investment for the company," it said.

Arakis shareholders, many of whom expected a big jump in the company's stock price following the announcement of the long-awaited Sudan deal, were disappointed by the stock's lackluster showing since the announcement early this month.

McLeod said the resignations and other moves showed Arakis had become more of a legitimate oil company since the deal to develop the project with China National Petroleum Corp, Malaysia state oil company Petronas and the Sudan government was revealed.
"The focus of the company changed when we signed this deal in Sudan, from a speculative stock," he said.
